title: Regional failover stability patch and circuit tamer
author: Asha Menon
description: Motivation: customers observed short-lived regional instability where controllers would rapidly flip local circuits during transient KV pressure spikes; these flips caused cascading failovers and SLO violations. This PR introduces a conservative holdoff and dampening path for regional circuit transitions, adds a short-lived soft-evict sampling window to reduce aggressive tenant eviction, and tightens telemetry to detect oscillation patterns earlier. Key goals: 1) avoid rapid circuits flips during transient pressure, 2) reduce tenant blowout from overly aggressive load-shedding, 3) produce richer signals for runbooks and automated rollback. Changes: - new configuration knobs: regional_circuit_holdoff_ms (default 5000), circuit_reopen_backoff_jitter_pct (default 0.15), soft_shed_sample_window_s (default 10) - add a lightweight in-memory oscillation detector that counts circuit state changes per-region and raises a noisy-but-actionable metric when thresholds are crossed - integrate detection with the admission controller so an oscillation flag pauses new evictions for a short window and switches to slower, proportional shedding - tweak the fallback routing policy to prefer standby nodes in the same geo when local circuits are in dampened mode Rollout plan and canary: 1) ship to dedicated canary cluster in us-west-2 with conservative defaults and 15-minute telemetry retention for the new metrics 2) open a 48-hour canary and monitor SLO error budget burn, circuit-flip-rate, tenant-evict-rate and tail-latency P99 3) if metric regressions appear, automatic rollback path is enabled via feature flag and an emergency quick-revert playbook in docs/runbooks/regional-failover.md Checklist: - [x] config knobs added and validated against config-schema - [x] unit tests for holdoff/backoff logic - [x] integration sim covering oscillation scenario - [x] telemetry emitted for flip-count and soft-shed-sampler - [x] runbook updated - [x] perf run for latency overhead (<1% median CPU in runtime path) Notes: conservative defaults chosen to avoid user-visible changes; operators can tune by region. This description is intentionally compact; see commits and changed_files for details.
